calls.title: Coffee run for the team
calls.role: your teammate at the office
phrases: drink it in the café or take it away
calls.end: Be right back with the coffee. See you in ten minutes!

t0.m: Hey! I'm going to grab a coffee for the team. Do you want something?
o: Yes, please! A latte, please.
No, thanks. I'm okay.
Sure! What do they have?
br: No problem! How about a snack, then?
They have coffee, tea, and hot chocolate.

t1.m: Do you want it hot or iced?
o: Iced, please. It's really hot today.
Hot, please.
Hmm, iced, I think.
br: Iced it is! It's so warm outside today.
Hot – perfect for this cold office!

t2.m: What size? Small, medium, or large?
o: Medium, please.
A large one, please. I'm very tired.
Small is fine, thanks.
Oat milk, please.
Regular milk is fine.
No milk, thanks.
br: Oat milk – nice. I like it too.

t4.m: Anything to eat? They have great muffins.
o: Yes, a blueberry muffin, please.
No, thank you. Just the coffee.
What kind of muffins do they have?
br: Blueberry and chocolate. The blueberry one is my favorite.

t5.m: Okay, that's it. It's my treat today!
o: Thank you so much! Next time it's on me.
Oh, thanks! That's very kind.
Are you sure? Let me pay.
br: Don't worry about it! You can pay next time.

calls.title: Monday chat about the weekend
calls.role: your friendly coworker
phrases: relax and do not work hard
calls.end: Have a great Monday!

t0.m: Good morning! How was your weekend?
o: It was great, thanks! How was yours?
It was good. I relaxed at home.
Not bad. A little busy.
br: Mine was great, thanks for asking!
Nice and relaxing, I love that.

t1.m: What did you do on Saturday?
o: I went to the beach with my friends.
I watched a movie and cooked dinner.
I visited my parents.
br: Wow, the weather was perfect for that!
Ooh, which movie did you see?

t2.m: Did you do anything on Sunday?
o: Not much. I just took it easy.
I cleaned my apartment and went shopping.
I played soccer in the morning.
br: Sometimes doing nothing is the best plan.

t3.m: I went to a food festival downtown. It was amazing!
o: That sounds fun! What did you eat?
Cool! Was it crowded?
I love food festivals!
br: Tacos, dumplings, and the best ice cream ever.

t4.m: Do you have any plans for next weekend?
o: Not yet. Do you have any ideas?
Yes, I'm going to visit a friend in Chicago.
I want to try that food festival!
br: You should check out the farmers market. It's great.
You should! It's on again next Saturday.
Oh, fun! Have a great time.

t5.m: Okay, I have a meeting now. Let's catch up at lunch!
o: Sure! See you at lunch.
Sounds good. Have a good meeting!
Okay, talk later!

calls.title: Your first day at a US office
calls.role: your new teammate, showing you around
phrases: you can do it without asking
calls.end: Great! I'll come get you at twelve thirty. Good luck with onboarding!

t0.m: Hi! You must be the new designer. I'm Ama. Welcome to the team!
o: Hi Ama, nice to meet you! Thanks for the welcome.
Hello! Yes, I'm the new designer. Nice to meet you.
Hi! I'm a bit nervous, but excited.
br: Don't worry, everyone here is really friendly.

t1.m: How was your trip to the office this morning?
o: It was easy. I took the subway.
A little stressful. The traffic was terrible.
Good! I walked here. I live close by.
br: Oh no! It gets better if you leave a bit earlier.
The subway is the fastest way, for sure.

t2.m: Let me show you around. This is the kitchen. The coffee is free, by the way.
o: Free coffee? That's great!
Thanks! Where can I find tea?
Nice. Can I bring my own lunch?
br: Tea is in the top cupboard, next to the mugs.
Of course! Just put your name on it in the fridge.
t2.re: Yep, it's the best perk here.

t3.m: And this is your desk. Your laptop is ready. Do you have any questions so far?
o: Yes. Who should I ask if I need help?
What time do people usually have lunch?
Not right now, thanks. Everything is clear.
br: You can always ask me, or our manager, Jordan.
Usually around twelve thirty. We often eat together.
Great. Feel free to ask me anything later.

t4.m: Your onboarding session starts at ten. Have you used our design tools before?
o: Yes, I used them at my last job.
Not really, but I learn fast.
Some of them. I'd love a quick tutorial.
br: No problem, you'll get the hang of it quickly.
Perfect, that will make it easier.

t5.m: A few of us are having lunch together today. Do you want to join us?
o: I'd love to! Thanks for inviting me.
Sure, what time?
Thanks, but I brought my own lunch today.
br: No worries! You can still sit with us in the kitchen.

calls.title: Quick daily stand-up update
calls.role: your team lead, running the stand-up
phrases: a problem that stops your work
calls.end: Okay, that's it for today. Have a productive day!

t0.m: Morning! Let's keep it quick. What did you work on yesterday?
o: Yesterday I finished the new login page.
I fixed two bugs in the payment form.
I worked on the report for the client.

t1.m: What are you working on today?
o: Today I'm going to test the login page.
I'm starting the user settings page.
I'll finish the client report this morning.
No blockers, everything is on track.
Yes, I'm waiting for the designs from Sam.
Kind of. I don't have access to the test server.
br: Okay, I'll ping Sam after this meeting.
I'll ask IT to give you access today.

t3.m: When do you think you can wrap up this task?
o: I think I can finish it by Thursday.
Probably by the end of the week.
It depends on the designs, maybe Friday.
br: Fair. Let me know as soon as you have them.

t4.m: Should I loop anyone else in?
o: Yes, please loop in the QA team.
No, I think we're fine for now.
Maybe Sam, for the designs.
br: Good idea, I'll add them to the thread.

t5.m: Great update. Anything else before we move on?
o: No, that's all from me. Thanks!
Just one thing: I'm off on Friday afternoon.
Nope, all good.
br: Thanks for the heads-up. Enjoy your afternoon off!

calls.title: Booking a doctor's appointment
calls.role: the receptionist at a local clinic
phrases: book a time to see someone
a card that shows your health insurance
tell the front desk you have arrived
calls.end: You're all set. See you tomorrow, and feel better soon!

t0.m: Good morning, Sunrise Family Clinic. This is Ama. How can I help you?
o: Hi, I'd like to make an appointment, please.
Hello, I need to see a doctor.
Hi, can I book a check-up?
t0.re: Of course, I can help with that.

t1.m: Are you a new patient, or have you been here before?
o: I'm a new patient.
I've been here before.
I'm new. I just moved to the area.
br: Welcome! I'll just need some basic information.

t2.m: And what's the reason for your visit?
o: I have a bad cough and a sore throat.
I just need a general check-up.
I've had a headache for three days.
br: I'm sorry to hear that. Let's get you in soon.
Oh, I'm sorry. We'll find a time quickly.

t3.m: The earliest available time is tomorrow at 9:30 a.m. Does that work for you?
o: Yes, 9:30 works for me.
Do you have anything in the afternoon?
Is there anything today?
br: We have 3:15 p.m. tomorrow. Is that better?
Sorry, today is fully booked. Tomorrow at 9:30 is the earliest.

t4.m: Can I have your full name and date of birth, please?
o: Sure. My name is Linh Tran. My birthday is May 2nd, 1995.
Yes, it's Linh Tran, May 2nd, 1995.
Of course. Do you need me to spell my name?
br: Yes, please – I want to get it right.

t5.m: Please bring your insurance card and a photo ID. Do you have any questions?
o: No, that's all. Thank you!
Should I come early to check in?
Where do I park?
br: Yes, please come ten minutes early to check in.
There's free parking behind the building.

calls.title: Calling about an apartment for rent
calls.role: a property manager with an apartment for rent
phrases: money you pay before moving in, returned later
water and electricity are part of the rent
book a time to see a place
calls.end: Perfect, I'll text you the address. See you then!

t0.m: Hi, this is Carlos from Maple Street Rentals. You called about the one-bedroom apartment?
o: Yes, hi! Is it still available?
Hi Carlos, yes. I saw the listing online.
Yes, I'm interested in the apartment on Maple Street.

t1.m: It's a sunny one-bedroom on the third floor. What would you like to know?
o: How much is the rent?
Is it close to public transportation?
Are utilities included?
br: Yes, the bus stop is right outside.
Water is included, but electricity isn't.

t2.m: Just so you know, there's a security deposit of one month's rent. Is that okay?
o: Yes, that's fine.
Is it refundable when I move out?
Could I pay it in two parts?
br: Yes, as long as there's no damage.
I'll have to check with the owner, but it may be possible.

t3.m: How long would you like the lease to be?
o: One year, ideally.
Do you offer six-month leases?
I'm not sure yet. What are the options?
br: We do, but the rent is a little higher.
We have six-month and twelve-month leases.

o: No, I don't have any pets.
Yes, I have a small cat. Is that okay?
Not now, but I might get a dog later.
br: The building is pet-friendly, so that's fine.

t5.m: Would you like to schedule a viewing?
o: Yes, please. Are you free on Saturday morning?
Sure! Is tomorrow evening possible?
Yes. What times are available?
br: Saturday at ten works for me.
I'm free tomorrow at six or Saturday at ten.

calls.title: IELTS Part 1: home, work and free time
calls.role: IELTS Speaking examiner (practice)
phrases: a natural way to start an honest answer
a soft way to give your opinion
partly one thing, partly the other

name.m: Good morning. My name is Ama. Can you tell me your full name, please?
o: My name is Linh Nguyen, but most people call me Linh.
I’m Minh. My full name is Tran Van Minh.
name.re: Thank you. Now, let’s talk about what you do.

job.m: Do you work, or are you a student?
o: I’m a student. I’m studying business at a university in Hanoi.
I work as a sales assistant in a bank, and I really enjoy it.
A bit of both, actually. I study in the morning and work part-time in the evening.

study.m: What do you like most about your studies?
o: I like my major because it is very practical, and my classmates are really friendly.
To be honest, I love the group projects, because I learn a lot from other people.

work.m: What do you like most about your job?
o: I’d say my colleagues. They are helpful, so I never feel stressed at work.
I like that every day is different, and I can meet new customers.

both.m: How do you manage your time between work and study?
o: I plan my week every Sunday, so I know when to study and when to work.
It’s not easy, but I use a calendar app and I study on the bus during my commute.

home.m: Let’s move on to your hometown. Where is your hometown?
o: My hometown is Da Nang, a coastal city in the centre of Vietnam.
I come from a small town near Hue. It’s quiet and very green.

live.m: Would you like to live there in the future? Why or why not?
o: Yes, I would, because the air is fresh, life is calm and my whole family lives there.
Probably not. It’s a lovely place, but there are more jobs in big cities.

free.m: Now let’s talk about free time. What do you usually do at the weekend?
o: When it comes to weekends, I usually relax at home, cook with my family and watch a film.
I’m into sports, so I play badminton with my friends on Saturday mornings.

prefer.m: Do you prefer spending free time alone or with other people?
o: I prefer spending time with friends, because we can share ideas and have fun together.
I’d say a bit of both. I like quiet time alone, but I also enjoy meeting friends.
prefer.re: Thank you. That’s the end of Part 1.

calls.end: Well done. You gave clear answers. Try to add a reason or an example to every answer.

calls.title: IELTS Part 2: describe a place you like to visit
calls.role: IELTS Speaking examiner (practice)
phrases: the best thing for me is…
it takes about … to get there
I really think you should go
it is good enough to visit

intro.m: Now I’m going to give you a topic. You have one minute to prepare, then talk for one to two minutes. Describe a place you like to visit.
cue: and explain why you like it
o: I’m ready.

talk.m: Remember to say where it is, how you get there, what you do there, and why you like it.
o: I’d like to talk about Hoi An, an old town that is located in central Vietnam. It takes about forty minutes to get there from Da Nang by bus. When I visit, I usually walk along the river, try local food and take photos of the lanterns. What I love most is the peaceful atmosphere in the evening, because the whole town is lit up and nobody is in a hurry. I first went there with my family when I was ten, so it’s a memorable place for me, and every visit brings back happy memories. Another reason I like it is that it’s not expensive: a bowl of local noodles costs only a dollar or two. Overall, it’s definitely worth a visit, and I’d highly recommend it to anyone.

often.m: How often do you go there?
o: About twice a year, usually in the summer holidays.
Not very often, maybe once a year, because it is quite far.

others.m: Would you recommend it to tourists?
o: Yes, definitely, but I’d suggest going early in the morning, because it gets crowded later.
I would, because the scenery is breathtaking and the local people are friendly.
others.re: Thank you. That’s the end of Part 2.

calls.end: Good job. In Part 2, try to keep talking for the full two minutes, and use your notes for each point.

calls.title: IELTS Part 3: technology and learning
calls.role: IELTS Speaking examiner (practice)
phrases: on the one hand… on the other hand…
something with good and bad sides

online.m: Let’s discuss technology and education. Do you think online learning is better than learning in a classroom?
o: It depends on the learner. On the one hand, online learning is convenient and cheap. On the other hand, many students need a teacher in the room to stay motivated.
To some extent, yes, because people can study anywhere. However, classroom learning gives more interaction, which is important for speaking skills.
br: depends|both|on the one hand|to some extent

young.m: Why do you think young people pick up new technology faster than older people?
o: I think young people grew up with smartphones, so technology feels natural to them. Older people often worry about making mistakes, which slows them down.
Mainly because of exposure. The younger generation uses apps every day at school, while many older people only started using them recently.

risk.m: What are the risks of children spending a lot of time on screens?
o: The biggest risk is distraction. Children may find it hard to focus on long tasks, and they spend less time playing outside, which is bad for their health.
Technology is a double-edged sword. It gives children access to information, but too much screen time can affect their sleep and their social skills.

future.m: How might technology change the way people learn in the future?
o: In the long run, I believe learning will be more personal. For example, apps could find each student’s weak points and give them the right practice.
I think teachers will still be important, but they will use technology to give faster feedback, so students can learn more efficiently.
future.re: Thank you. That’s the end of the speaking test.

calls.end: Well done. In Part 3, give your opinion, a reason and an example, and compare both sides when you can.

calls.title: TOEIC: rescheduling a client meeting
calls.role: office manager at a client company
phrases: a polite way to give bad news
is … a good time for you?
I’ll send you a calendar invite
I will email the meeting time

hello.m: Good afternoon, Bright Office Supplies, this is Ama speaking. How can I help you?
o: Hello, this is Linh from Green Tech. I’m calling about our meeting on Thursday.
Hi Ama, I’m afraid I need to reschedule our appointment this week.
br: Yes, I have it here: Thursday at ten.
hello.re: Sure, what can I do for you?

why.m: May I ask why you need to change the time?
o: I have a schedule conflict. Our director called an urgent meeting at the same time.
I’m afraid I have to attend a conference on Thursday morning.

when.m: When would you be available instead?
o: Would Friday at two p.m. work for you?
I’m available on Monday morning, any time after nine.
br: Let me double-check… Friday at two is fine.
Monday morning… we have ten o’clock free.
Let me see… that should be possible.
when.re: Let me see… I can offer Friday at two.

confirm.m: Shall I send you a calendar invite to confirm the new time?
o: Yes, please. Could you send it to my work email?
That would be great, thank you. Sorry for the inconvenience.

extra.m: Is there anything else I can help you with today?
o: Yes, could you also send me the invoice before the deadline on Friday?
No, that’s everything. Thank you for your help.
br: Sure, I’ll attach the invoice to the email.

calls.end: Thank you for calling. Have a great afternoon!

calls.title: At the bakery
calls.role: friendly baker
phrases: you do not need to give me money back
I do not want anything else

hi.m: Good morning! Welcome to Sunny Bakery. What can I get you today?
o: Could I have a loaf of bread, please?
Hi! I’d like two croissants, please.
What do you recommend?
br: Our sourdough bread is freshly baked this morning!
Great choice, they are still warm.

bread.m: Would you like the bread sliced or whole?
o: Sliced, please.
Whole is fine, thanks.
br: No problem, I’ll slice it for you.

sweet.m: Anything sweet? The chocolate cake is very popular.
o: Yes, one slice of chocolate cake, please.
No, thank you. Just the bread.

drink.m: Would you like a coffee with that?
o: No, thanks. That’s all.
Yes, a small black coffee, please.

pay.m: That’s eight dollars fifty, please. Do you need a bag?
o: Yes, please. Here’s ten dollars.
No, thanks, I have my own bag. Can I pay by card?
br: Of course, just tap your card here.
Thank you! Here’s your change and your receipt.

calls.end: Enjoy your bread, and have a lovely day!

calls.title: Talking about your hobbies
calls.role: a friendly new classmate
phrases: when I am not working or studying
a way to ask the same question back

hi.m: Hi! Nice to meet you. What do you like to do in your free time?
o: I like to read books and listen to music.
I play football with my friends.
I like cooking. It is fun.
br: Cool! Sports are good for you.

often.m: How often do you do that?
o: I do it every weekend.
Almost every day, after work.
Once a week, on Sunday.
br: Wow, every day! You really love it.

start.m: When did you start? Was it a long time ago?
o: I started two years ago.
I started when I was a child.
It is new. I started last month.
br: So you have done it for many years. Impressive!
Oh, so it is new! How is it going?
Two years is a good time to get better.

who.m: Do you do it alone, or with other people?
o: I do it with my friends.
I usually do it alone. I like quiet time.
Sometimes alone, sometimes with my brother.
br: Quiet time is important. I understand.
It is more fun with other people!

you.m: I love hiking and taking photos. Do you want to try something new?
o: Yes, I want to try hiking. It sounds fun.
Maybe. What do I need for it?
Not now, but maybe next year.
br: Just comfortable shoes and water. That is all!
No problem. You can think about it.
Great! We can go together one day.

close.m: Well, I have to go to class. What about you? Any plan for this weekend?
o: I will play football with my friends.
I want to stay home and rest.
I will go shopping and see a movie.
close.re: That sounds like a good weekend!

calls.end: It was nice talking to you. See you in class!

calls.title: Tell me about your family
calls.role: a new friend who is curious about your family
phrases: There are four people in my family.
how to say the size of your family
how to tell a person’s job

size.m: Hello! I would like to know about your family. How many people are there?
o: There are four people in my family.
There are five of us: my parents, my sister, and me.
It is a small family. Only three people.
br: A small family can be very close.
That is a big family! It must be lively.

live.m: Do you all live in the same house?
o: Yes, we all live together.
No. My brother lives in another city.
I live with my parents. My sister lives abroad.
br: It is hard to be far from family. Do you call often?
I think living together is nice.

parents.m: What do your parents do? Do they work?
o: My father is a driver, and my mother is a nurse.
My mother works in a shop. My father is retired.
They both work in an office.
br: He must enjoy his free time.
Sounds like a busy day for them.

siblings.m: Do you have any brothers or sisters?
o: Yes, I have one older sister.
I have a younger brother. He is ten years old.
No, I am an only child.
br: Being an only child has good things, too.

together.m: Do you get along well with your family?
o: Yes, we get along very well.
Most of the time, yes. Sometimes we argue.
Yes. We have dinner together every day.
br: That is normal in every family.
Family meals are a lovely habit.
I am happy to hear that.

tell.m: Tell me one thing you like to do with your family.
o: We like to go to the park on Sunday.
We love to cook and eat together.
We watch movies at home on Friday night.
tell.re: That sounds like a special time.

calls.end: Thanks for sharing. Your family sounds wonderful!

calls.title: Your favourite food
calls.role: a friend planning a dinner
phrases: I really do not like something
a food that makes you sick

fav.m: I want to cook a nice dinner this weekend. What is your favourite food?
o: My favourite dish is noodle soup.
I love pizza, especially with mushrooms.
I really like rice with chicken and vegetables.

made.m: Oh, I want to try it! What is it made with?
o: It is made with noodles, beef, and fresh herbs.
You need flour, tomatoes, and cheese.
It has rice, chicken, and a little oil.

taste.m: How does it taste? Is it sweet, salty, or spicy?
o: It tastes salty and a bit spicy.
It is not spicy. It is rich and a little sweet.
It is fresh and light.
br: Oh, I can handle some spice, but not too much.

learn.m: Who taught you to cook it? Or do you eat it at a restaurant?
o: My mother taught me. I cook it at home.
I learned from a video online.
I do not cook. I eat it at a small restaurant near my home.

dislike.m: Is there any food you can’t stand?
o: I can’t stand very sweet desserts.
I do not like fish. The smell is strong.
I eat almost everything, but not onions.
br: Oh, thank you for telling me. I will be careful.
That makes it easy to cook for you!

invite.m: Great. Would you like to come to my dinner on Saturday?
o: Yes, I would love to. What can I bring?
Thank you! I would like that.
I am sorry, I am busy on Saturday. Maybe Sunday?
br: No problem. Let us find another day.
Just bring a dessert, if you like.

calls.end: Perfect. I can’t wait. See you on Saturday!

calls.title: Planning a trip together
calls.role: a friend who wants to travel with you
phrases: What do you have in mind?
not spending a lot of money
a place that is not very touristy

where.m: I’d love to take a short trip this summer. Where would you like to go?
o: I’d like to visit a small coastal town.
I’m thinking about the mountains. I need fresh air.
Somewhere with lots of history, maybe an old city.
br: The sea sounds perfect in summer.
Nature is a great way to relax.

when.m: How long can you be away? A weekend, or maybe a full week?
o: I can take about five days.
Only a long weekend. I’m busy at work.
A week would be great, if we plan early.
br: A long weekend is easy to plan.
That is enough time to enjoy it.

budget.m: Let’s talk about money. Do you want to travel on a budget, or spend more for comfort?
o: I prefer to travel on a budget, but I want a clean hotel.
I’m okay to spend more for a nice room.
Let’s keep it cheap. I’d rather spend money on food.
br: Okay, we can find good deals.
Sure, a little comfort is nice after a long day.

stay.m: What kind of place should we book? A hotel, an apartment, or a small guesthouse?
o: A small guesthouse sounds friendly and cheap.
An apartment is better. We can cook there.
A hotel with breakfast, please. It is easy.
br: Guesthouses are cosy, and the owners know good places.
Good thinking, it saves money too.
Breakfast included is always a plus.

do.m: What do you want to do there? Do you prefer famous places or somewhere off the beaten path?
o: I prefer places off the beaten path. They are quieter.
I want to see the famous places first, then explore.
I want to eat local food and walk around slowly.
br: Me too. Local places give the real feeling of a city.
Good plan. We should not miss the famous ones.

pack.m: Last thing: we should pack light. Do you have any worry before we book?
o: My only worry is the weather. Let’s check it first.
No worries. I can book the tickets tonight.
I’m a little worried about the price of flights.
br: Good point. I’ll check the forecast tonight.
Let’s look at the prices tomorrow and compare.
Great! I’ll book the room at the same time.

calls.end: This will be fun. I’ll send you some ideas tomorrow!

calls.title: Chatting about a movie you just saw
calls.role: a friend who loves movies
phrases: a simple way to start a summary
I couldn’t take my eyes off…
it was very interesting to watch
it was a good use of time
you suggest it to some people

seen.m: Hey! I heard you watched a movie last night. What was it?
o: I watched a comedy about two friends on a road trip.
It was a science fiction movie. The title is hard to say.
I saw a love story. My friend chose it.
br: Ha! I need a good comedy.

about.m: What is it about? Try not to spoil the ending!
o: It’s about a woman who leaves her job to travel.
It’s about two brothers who find a secret map.
It’s about a robot that learns to feel emotions.

plot.m: How was the plot? Was it easy to follow?
o: The plot was simple, but it kept me interested.
It was a little confusing in the middle.
Yes, the story was clear and exciting.
br: Confusing plots can be annoying. Did it get better?
That is the best kind of story.

actors.m: And the actors? Did they do a good job?
o: The main actor was excellent. I loved his voice.
The acting was good, but the music was even better.
They were okay, but I did not feel the emotions.
br: Good music can change a whole scene.
It is hard to enjoy a story without feeling something.

end.m: So, was it worth watching? Would you recommend it?
o: Yes, I’d recommend it to anyone who likes comedy.
It was good, but not great. Watch it at home.
Definitely! I want to watch it again.
br: Now I really want to see it!
Thanks for being honest. Maybe I’ll wait for streaming.
Great, I’ll watch it this weekend.

next.m: What kind of movie do you want to watch next?
o: I’d like to watch a documentary about nature.
Maybe something scary, if you come with me.
Anything with a good story.
next.re: Let’s plan a movie night soon!

calls.end: Thanks for the review. Let’s watch something together soon!

calls.title: Your morning routine
calls.role: a roommate curious about your mornings
phrases: the normal time you wake up
while I travel to my job
sleep a little longer after the alarm

up.m: Morning! You are up early today. What time do you usually get up?
o: I usually get up at six thirty.
Around seven. I’m not a morning person.
Very early, at five, to exercise.
br: Ha! Same. The alarm is my enemy.

alarm.m: Do you wake up easily, or do you hit the snooze button?
o: I hit the snooze button two or three times.
I wake up before my alarm. It is strange.
It depends. I wake up easily if I sleep well.
br: I do that too, and then I am in a hurry.
You are lucky. Good sleep is a gift.

first.m: What is the first thing you do after you get up?
o: First, I drink a glass of water and open the window.
I check my phone. I know it is a bad habit.
I make a cup of tea and sit quietly.
br: Many people do that. Try putting it away for ten minutes.

ready.m: How long do you need to get ready?
o: It takes me about thirty minutes.
I am fast. Only fifteen minutes.
About an hour. I like to take my time.

breakfast.m: Do you eat breakfast at home? What do you usually have?
o: I usually have toast with eggs and fruit.
I do not have time. I grab something on my way to work.
I always have a big breakfast. It gives me energy.
br: Try to eat something. It helps you focus.
That sounds like a healthy breakfast.

leave.m: And how do you go to work? Is it far?
o: I take the bus. It takes about forty minutes.
I ride my bike. It is only ten minutes.
I walk. It is close, so I can listen to music.
leave.re: Nice, a good start to the day.

calls.end: Thanks! Now I want a coffee. Have a great day!

calls.title: Your English learning journey
calls.role: a language exchange partner
phrases: get out of my comfort zone

long.m: Hi! Thanks for joining our exchange. How long have you been learning English?
o: I’ve been learning English for about three years.
Only six months, but I study every day.
Since school, but I stopped for a while.
br: It is never too late to start again.

why.m: Why did you decide to learn English?
o: I need it for my job. My company works with other countries.
I want to travel and talk to people easily.
I love English songs and movies. I want to understand them.
br: English can really open doors at work.
Travelling is the best reason to practise.
That is a fun way to learn!

hard.m: What do you find most difficult: speaking, listening, reading, or writing?
o: Speaking is the most difficult for me. I get nervous.
Listening is hard because people speak fast.
Grammar is hard. There are so many rules.
br: Many learners feel that. Talking like this helps a lot.
Try slow podcasts first, then faster ones.
Grammar is easier in small steps.

method.m: What do you do to practise? Any method that works well for you?
o: I watch short videos and repeat the sentences.
I read a little every day and write new words in a notebook.
I talk with a friend online twice a week.
br: A word notebook helps you remember.
Real conversation is the best practice.

mistake.m: Do you worry about making mistakes when you speak?
o: Yes, a little. I stop when I am not sure.
Not so much now. I know mistakes help me learn.
Sometimes. I feel embarrassed with strangers.
br: Exactly. Mistakes are proof that you are trying.
That is normal. Please keep going. I understand you very well.

goal.m: Last question: what is your goal for English in one year?
o: I want to speak with confidence at work meetings.
My goal is to pass an English exam.
I want to watch a movie without subtitles.
goal.re: That is a clear and realistic goal.

calls.end: You are doing great. Step by step, you will reach it!

calls.title: Weather and seasons
calls.role: a neighbour chatting at the bus stop
phrases: I am excited about something coming
a simple piece of advice for rain

today.m: Hi there! Beautiful day, isn’t it? What do you think of the weather today?
o: It is lovely today. The sky is blue and it is warm.
It is too hot for me. I can’t stand this heat.
It looks cloudy. I think it will rain later.
br: It is really hot. Drink lots of water!
You may be right. Better take an umbrella.

forecast.m: Did you check the forecast for the weekend?
o: Yes, it says it will be sunny on Saturday.
No, I did not. Is it going to rain?
I heard it will be windy and cold.
br: They say there will be rain on Sunday.
Then I will stay at home with a book.

favorite.m: Which season do you like best? Why?
o: I like autumn best because the weather is cool and calm.
Summer, because I can go swimming.
Spring is my favourite because the flowers come out.
br: Summer is great, but I don’t like the crowds.
The colours of autumn are beautiful.
Winter is cosy with hot drinks!

worst.m: And which season do you like least?
o: I like winter the least. It is dark and cold.
I don’t like summer because it is too hot.
I do not mind any season. I like them all.
br: You are very easy to please!
Short days make me tired too.
Same here. I need air conditioning.

wear.m: What do you wear on a rainy or cold day?
o: I wear a warm jacket and boots, and I bring an umbrella.
A coat, a scarf, and gloves.
I wear a raincoat and carry a small umbrella.

plans.m: So what are you doing this weekend if the weather is nice?
o: If it is sunny, I will go to the park with my friends.
I will visit my grandmother and cook with her.
I will clean my house, no matter the weather.
plans.re: That sounds like a nice weekend!

calls.end: My bus is here. Enjoy the weather, and see you around!

calls.title: Calling about an online order
calls.role: a customer service agent at an online store

hello.m: Thank you for calling Bluebird Store. This is Ama. How can I help you today?
o: Hi, I placed an order last week, and it hasn’t arrived yet.
Hello, I received my order, but one item is damaged.
Hi, I ordered the wrong size. Can I exchange it?
br: I’m sorry about the delay. Let me check.
Oh no, I’m very sorry about that.
No problem, we can help with that.

number.m: Could you give me your order number, please? You can find it in your email.
o: Sure. It is B, one, two, seven, four, nine.
One moment, please. I am looking for it. Okay, it is four, five, eight, two.
I can’t find the email. Can I give you my name instead?
br: Of course. Please spell your last name for me.

detail.m: I see your order. Can you tell me what happened in detail?
o: I ordered a blue jacket in size medium on Monday, and I haven’t had any news.
The cup in the box was broken, and there is a crack on the side.
The jacket is too small. I need a larger size.
br: I understand. We can send a bigger size.
That should not happen. We will fix it.
The package is with the courier. It should arrive tomorrow.

solution.m: I can offer you a replacement, or a full refund. Which would you prefer?
o: I’d prefer a replacement, please.
A refund, please. I don’t need it anymore.
Can I wait for the delivery first? If it is late, I want a refund.
br: Of course. Please call us if it is late tomorrow.
Sure. The money will return in three to five days.
We will send a new one for free.

when.m: Is there a time that is good for you to receive the delivery?
o: I’m at home in the evening, after six.
Please deliver it before noon. I work in the afternoon.
Anytime is fine. My neighbour can take it.

more.m: Is there anything else I can help you with today?
o: No, that’s all. Thank you for your help.
Yes, can I get a confirmation by email?
Could you tell me how to track my package next time?
br: Sure. Use the link in your email, and enter the order number.
Of course. You will get it in a few minutes.

calls.end: Thank you for calling Bluebird Store. Have a great day!

calls.title: Your goals for this year
calls.role: a friend at a New Year’s gathering
phrases: decide what you want to achieve
step out of my comfort zone

goal.m: The new year is here! Do you have any goals for this year?
o: Yes, my main goal this year is to learn to speak English fluently.
I want to save money for a big trip.
I’m aiming to be healthier and exercise more.
br: That is a great goal. I’ll help you if I can.
A trip is a good reason to save.

why.m: Why is that important to you?
o: Because I want a better job, and I need English for it.
It makes me happy, and I feel stronger.
I want to feel proud of myself at the end of the year.

plan.m: How do you plan to reach it? What is your first step?
o: My first step is to practise twenty minutes every day.
I’ll make a monthly budget and put aside some money each week.
I’ll join a gym near my house and go three times a week.
br: Small daily steps are better than big, rare ones.
A budget is a good tool.

stick.m: It is easy to start, but hard to stick to a plan. What will you do when you feel lazy?
o: I will remind myself why I started and try a small step anyway.
I will ask a friend to check on me every week.
I will take a short rest, then continue the next day.
br: A rest is fine, as long as you come back.
Reminding yourself of the reason is powerful.

track.m: How will you keep track of your progress?
o: I’ll write in a notebook every night.
I’ll use an app to see my progress each week.
I’ll put a mark on the calendar every day I do it.
track.re: That is a nice and simple system.

last.m: What was your biggest success last year? Tell me one thing you are proud of.
o: Last year I finished a hard course, and I am proud of it.
I learned to cook, and now I cook for my family.
I changed jobs. It was scary, but it was a good decision.
br: Changing jobs takes courage. Well done!
That is a useful skill and a kind gift.
Finishing something hard is a big win.

calls.end: I believe you can do it. Happy New Year, and good luck!

calls.title: A childhood memory
calls.role: a friend sharing old memories
phrases: it makes you remember the past
the past was a happy time

grow.m: Looking at old photos made me think of my childhood. Where did you grow up?
o: I grew up in a small town near the sea.
I grew up in a big city, in a small apartment.
I grew up in a village. Everyone knew each other.
br: Growing up by the sea sounds magical.
Villages are friendly. I like that.
Cities have a lot of energy.

play.m: What did you use to do after school when you were little?
o: I used to play outside with my friends until dinner time.
I used to help my grandmother in the garden.
I used to read comic books in my room.
br: A quiet child with a big imagination!
Those were the days! No phones, only games.

toy.m: Do you remember your favourite toy or game?
o: I remember my red bicycle. I rode it every day.
I loved a small teddy bear. I took it everywhere.
My favourite game was hide and seek.
br: A bike gives you a feeling of freedom.
I had one too! It felt like a friend.
Simple games can be the most fun.

school.m: And what was school like? Did you enjoy it?
o: I enjoyed it. My favourite teacher made learning fun.
It was difficult sometimes, but I had great friends.
Not really. I was shy, and I preferred to stay home.
br: Many children feel that way. You turned out great!
A good teacher stays in our memory forever.

never.m: Is there a moment from your childhood that you will never forget?
o: I’ll never forget the day my father taught me to swim.
I’ll never forget my first trip with my family to the mountains.
I’ll never forget the smell of my grandmother’s kitchen.
br: First trips make a deep impression.
Smells bring back memories so strongly.
never.re: It brings back memories, doesn’t it?

now.m: Do you think children today have a different childhood from yours?
o: Yes, I think children today spend more time with screens.
In some ways, yes, but they still love to play.
I think they have more opportunities, but less freedom.

calls.end: Thanks for sharing. It was lovely to remember the old days!

calls.title: Your dream job
calls.role: a mentor talking about careers
phrases: a good mix of work and personal time
I would be very happy to
it depends on one main thing

dream.m: Let’s talk about careers. If you could do any job in the world, what would it be?
o: If I could choose, I would be a travel photographer.
I would love to be a teacher, because I enjoy helping people learn.
I’d start my own company and work for myself.
br: That is a creative path. Very inspiring.
Being your own boss is brave.

why.m: What attracts you most about that job?
o: What attracts me is the freedom. Every day would be different.
I want a job that makes a positive difference to people.
I would like to be creative, rather than doing the same task all day.
why.re: That says a lot about what matters to you.

skills.m: What skills or qualifications would you need to get there?
o: I would need strong technical skills and a good portfolio.
I’d need a degree, and also patience and good communication.
I would need business knowledge, and the courage to take risks.
br: Study is a strong start. Do you have a plan?
Real experience is often more important than a certificate.
Courage is a skill you can learn.

gap.m: And what is the biggest gap between where you are and that dream?
o: The biggest gap is experience. I need to start working on small projects.
It’s mostly money. I need savings before I can change careers.
Honestly, it is confidence. I don’t believe I’m good enough yet.
br: Many successful people felt the same. Start small, and it grows.
That is a practical problem. A part-time start could help.
Small projects are the best way. Even one a month.
gap.re: It helps to be honest about that.

balance.m: How important is work-life balance for you compared to salary?
o: For me, balance is more important than a high salary.
I think salary matters when you’re young, but balance matters later.
I want both, but I’d choose a job I love over a big salary.
br: Good point. Priorities change over time.
A job you love is worth a lot.
Time is the one thing we cannot buy back.

step.m: What is one thing you could do this month to move closer to your dream?
o: I could talk to someone who already does the job and ask for advice.
I could take an online course in the evening.
I could start a small project and show it to my friends.
step.re: A small step, but a smart one. That is how careers are built.

calls.end: I think you will get there. It’s a matter of patience and practice. Good luck!

calls.title: Asking for directions
calls.role: a friendly local on the street
phrases: a polite way to ask for a place

hi.m: Hello! You look a little lost. Can I help you?
o: Yes, please. Where is the station?
Excuse me, where is the bank?
Yes. I am looking for the post office.
br: The station is not far from here.
hi.re: Okay, I think I can help.

far.m: It is about five minutes on foot. Do you want to walk, or take the bus?
o: I want to walk, please.
I prefer the bus.
Is it far from here?
br: Good. It is a nice street.
The bus stop is over there, next to the café.
No, it is close. Only five minutes.

route.m: Go straight on this street. Then turn left at the traffic lights. Okay?
o: Go straight, then turn left at the lights.
Straight on, and turn left at the traffic lights.
Sorry, can you say it again, please?
br: Of course! Go straight. Then turn left at the lights. Slowly: straight… then left.

where.m: The place is on the right, next to a small pharmacy. Is that clear?
o: Yes, it is clear. Thank you.
It is next to the pharmacy, right?
Sorry, what is a pharmacy?
br: A pharmacy is a shop for medicine. It has a green cross.

why.m: By the way, are you here on holiday, or for work?
o: I am here on holiday.
I am here for work. I work in a hotel.
I am a student. I study English here.
br: Welcome! I hope you enjoy our city.
Nice. I hope work goes well.
Great! English is a good thing to learn.

calls.end: Good luck! Enjoy your day.

calls.title: Buying a bus ticket
calls.role: a ticket seller at the bus station
phrases: a ticket to go and come back

hi.m: Good morning. Where would you like to go?
o: One ticket to Hue, please.
I want a ticket to the airport.
Two tickets to Dalat, please.
One way, please.
Return, please. I come back on Sunday.
A return ticket, please.
br: A return ticket. Good. When do you come back?

time.m: The next bus leaves at ten thirty. Is that okay?
o: Yes, ten thirty is fine.
Is there a bus earlier than that?
What time does it arrive?
br: There is one at nine, but it is full today.
It arrives at one o’clock, about two and a half hours.

price.m: That is twelve dollars. How would you like to pay?
o: I want to pay by card, please.
Can I pay in cash?
How much is it for a student?
br: With a student card, it is ten dollars. Do you have one?
Yes, you can pay by card. Please put it here.

platform.m: Here is your ticket. Do you have any other questions?
o: Yes. Where is the platform?
Where can I wait for the bus?
No, thank you. That is all.
br: Go through the door on your left. It is platform four.

calls.end: Have a good trip!

calls.title: Checking in at a hotel
calls.role: a receptionist at a small hotel
phrases: ask if breakfast is in the price
Could I have a quiet room?

hi.m: Good evening, and welcome to the Garden Hotel. Do you have a reservation?
o: Yes, I have a reservation under the name Lee.
Yes. I booked a room for two nights.
No, I do not have one. Do you have a free room?
br: Let me check. Yes, we have one room left.
Thank you. I can see it on my screen.

nights.m: How many nights are you staying with us?
o: I am staying for three nights.
Just one night. I leave tomorrow morning.
I would like to stay for a week.
br: A whole week! I hope you enjoy our city.
One night, I see. Early start tomorrow?
Good. That is a nice amount of time.

breakfast.m: Here is your key, room 304 on the third floor. Do you have any questions?
o: Yes. Is breakfast included in the price?
What is the Wi-Fi password, please?
What time is check-out tomorrow?
br: Yes, breakfast is included. It is from seven to ten, on the first floor.
The password is on your key card. The Wi-Fi is free.

room.m: The room faces the street. Would you like a quieter room at the back?
o: Yes, please. I would like a quiet room.
No, the street is fine. I like the view.
Is the back room bigger or smaller?
br: It is a little smaller, but much quieter.
No problem. Room 312 is at the back. Here is the new key.

help.m: Is there anything else I can help you with tonight?
o: Yes. Can you recommend a good restaurant near here?
Could you call a taxi for me tomorrow at seven?
No, that is everything. Thank you very much.
br: There is a nice place on the corner. Just a two-minute walk.
Of course. I will book it for seven.

calls.end: Enjoy your stay. Good night!

calls.title: At the pharmacy
calls.role: a pharmacist who helps you
phrases: How long have you had it?
Take one tablet twice a day.
a thing that makes me sick
ask if a doctor is needed

hi.m: Hello! How can I help you today?
o: I have a sore throat and a cough.
I have a bad headache. I feel tired.
My stomach hurts and I feel sick.
br: A headache can be very tiring.
That is not nice. Let me ask you a few questions.

long.m: How long have you had this problem?
o: I have had it for two days.
Since yesterday evening.
Only a few hours. It started this morning.
br: That is quite a long time. Maybe you need a doctor.
It started today, so it is probably nothing serious.

fever.m: Do you have a fever? Do you feel hot or very cold?
o: No, I do not have a fever.
Yes, I feel hot. I think I have a fever.
I am not sure. I did not check my temperature.
br: Please check your temperature at home. If it is over thirty-eight, see a doctor.
Good. That is a good sign.

allergy.m: Are you allergic to any medicine?
o: No, I am not allergic to anything.
Yes. I am allergic to penicillin.
I think I am allergic to aspirin.
br: Thank you for telling me. I will give you something safe.

advice.m: Take one tablet twice a day, after food. Drink lots of water and rest. Do you have any questions?
o: Should I see a doctor if it gets worse?
How many days should I take the tablets?
Can I drink coffee with this medicine?
br: Yes. If you do not feel better in three days, please see a doctor.
Take them for five days, even if you feel better.
Coffee is fine, but water is better. Please avoid alcohol.

calls.end: I hope you feel better soon. Take care!

calls.title: A problem at the restaurant
calls.role: a waiter who wants to fix the problem

hi.m: Hello, is everything all right with your meal?
o: Excuse me, there is a problem with my order.
I ordered chicken, but I got fish.
The soup is cold. Can you help me?
br: Oh, I am so sorry. I think we mixed up the orders.
Oh dear. I will take it back to the kitchen.
hi.re: Oh, I am sorry about that.

fix.m: What would you like me to do? I can change it, or you can choose something else.
o: Could you change it, please? I would like the chicken.
I would like something else, please. What do you recommend?
Can I just have a salad instead?
br: Our pasta is very popular today.
Of course. A salad is quick to prepare.
Of course. I will tell the kitchen right away.

wait.m: It will take about ten minutes. Is that okay for you?
o: Yes, I can wait ten minutes.
Ten minutes is too long. I have a meeting.
That is fine. Can I have some water in the meantime?
br: I understand. I will ask the chef to make it fast.
Of course. I will bring it now.

bill.m: To say sorry, the drink is free today. Would you like anything else?
o: Thank you, that is very kind. Could I have the bill, please?
That is kind of you. I would like a coffee, please.
Thank you. Can I pay by card?
br: Of course. I will bring it to your table.
Certainly. I will bring it right away.

calls.end: Thank you for your patience. We hope to see you again!

calls.title: Apologising for being late
calls.role: a friend who has been waiting for you
phrases: admit what you could do better
Let me make it up to you.

hi.m: Hi… I have been waiting for forty minutes. What happened?
o: I am so sorry that I am late. I got stuck in traffic.
I am really sorry. My bus broke down on the way.
I apologise. I lost track of time at work.
br: Yes, the roads are terrible today.
I understand work can be busy.

call.m: Okay, but why did you not call or send me a message? I was worried.
o: You are right. I should have called you.
My phone battery died, so I could not send a message.
I did not want to disturb you. I was wrong.
br: That is annoying, but I would still like you to find a way to tell me.
Thank you for admitting that. It helps.

plan.m: We have missed the start of the film now. What should we do?
o: Let us see the next show. I will buy the tickets.
Maybe we can have dinner instead. It is my treat.
We could go to the park for a walk and talk.
br: Dinner sounds nice. I am quite hungry actually.
The next show is at nine. That could work.
A walk would be pleasant. The weather is nice.

promise.m: Alright. How can I be sure this will not happen again?
o: I promise I will leave earlier next time.
From now on, I will send you a message if I am going to be late.
It will not happen again. I will check the traffic before I leave.
promise.re: Thank you. I accept your apology. Let us enjoy the evening.

calls.end: Come on, let us go. I forgive you this time!

calls.title: Missed your flight
calls.role: an airline agent on the phone
phrases: I could not catch the next flight
Could you put me on the next flight?

hi.m: Thank you for calling Skyline Airways. This is Carlos. How can I help you?
o: Hello. I missed my connecting flight because the first one was late.
Hi, I missed my flight to Berlin. I need to change my ticket.
My flight was cancelled and I do not know what to do.
br: I am very sorry about the cancellation. Let me look at your booking.
I understand. Delays happen, and I will help you.
Let me see what we can do.
hi.re: Let me help you with that.

details.m: Could you give me your booking number and tell me where you are going?
o: The booking number is K, L, nine, four, two, and I am going to Berlin.
I am travelling to Madrid. I can send the number by message.
Sorry, I do not have the number. My name is on the booking.
br: No problem. I can find it with your name.
Thank you. I have it here.

option.m: The next flight is tomorrow morning at eight. There is also one tonight, but it costs more. Which do you prefer?
o: I prefer the flight tomorrow morning. Is there an extra charge?
I would take the one tonight, if the price is not too high.
Is there another flight today with a different airline?
br: Because the delay was ours, there is no extra charge for the morning flight.
We cannot book other airlines, but I can check our partners.
It costs sixty euros more. I can offer you a discount.

hotel.m: You will need to stay overnight. Do you need any help with that?
o: Yes, could you recommend a hotel near the airport?
Will the airline pay for the hotel and the meals?
What happens to my luggage? It is on the other plane.
br: Your luggage will arrive on the same flight as you, so you do not need to worry.
Yes, we can offer you a voucher for a hotel and dinner.
There is a hotel five minutes away. I will give you the name.

confirm.m: I have changed your booking. Is there anything else you need?
o: Could you send me the new ticket by email, so I have it in writing?
Yes, please confirm the time of the flight again, so I do not make a mistake.
No, that is all. Thank you for being so helpful.
confirm.re: Done. You will get an email in a few minutes.

calls.end: I apologise again for the problem. Have a safe flight tomorrow!

calls.title: Sharing the costs with friends
calls.role: a friend who organised a weekend trip

hi.m: Hi! The weekend was great. Now we need to talk about the money. The total for the house, food and petrol was four hundred and eighty dollars.
o: Thanks for organising it. Let us split it equally between the four of us.
That seems fair. How much does each person pay?
Can I see the receipts, please? I want to check the total.
br: Of course! I will send photos of all the receipts.
Four people, so one hundred and twenty each.
It is one hundred and twenty each, if we split it equally.

detail.m: Well… Tom did not come on Saturday, so he did not eat dinner with us. Is it fair that he pays the same?
o: I think he should pay less for the food, but the same for the house.
It is not very fair. Maybe he can pay ten dollars less.
I do not mind. It is easier if everyone pays the same.
br: That sounds reasonable. I will calculate it.
You are kind. Simple is good.

me.m: And I paid for the petrol on my card, so some of you owe me more. How shall we do it?
o: I owe you one hundred and twenty. I can transfer it today.
Could you send me your bank details, and I will pay you back tonight?
How about we pay you by the end of the week?
br: Great! That is the quickest way.
That is fine, but please do not forget.
I will send them right after this call.

next.m: We should plan the next trip soon. How do you want to handle the money next time?
o: Next time, let us each pay a small amount in advance, so nobody has to pay everything.
I suggest an app to track who paid for what. It is easier for everyone.
We could take turns to pay, and share the bill at the end.
br: An app is a great idea. I know a free one.
Good idea. It stops one person paying everything.

calls.end: Brilliant. Thanks for being so easy to deal with. Talk soon!

calls.title: A short job interview
calls.role: a hiring manager at a small company
phrases: I have two years of experience in…
I work well in a team.

hi.m: Good morning, and thanks for coming. Let us start. Can you tell me a little about yourself and your experience?
o: I have two years of experience in customer service. I enjoy helping people.
I recently finished university, and I did an internship at a travel company.
I worked in a shop for three years, and now I want a new challenge.
br: Good. An internship gives real experience.
That is useful experience for this role.

strength.m: What would you say is your biggest strength?
o: I am good at solving problems, and I stay calm under pressure.
My biggest strength is communication. I listen carefully before I answer.
I am very organised, so I finish my tasks on time.
br: That is very useful in this job.
Good communication is important for our team.

weak.m: And what is something you are still learning to do better?
o: I am still learning to say no when I am too busy. I am working on it.
Sometimes I spend too long on small details, but I now use a timer.
My English presentation skills are not perfect yet, so I take a course.
br: I like that you are taking action.
Good, you have a plan to improve.

team.m: Can you tell me about a time when you worked in a team and had a disagreement?
o: Once, a colleague and I disagreed about a plan. We talked it through and found a middle way.
In my last job, we had different ideas. I listened first, and then I explained mine.
I try to avoid conflict, but I once asked my manager to help us decide.
br: Asking for help at the right time shows maturity.
That is a mature way to deal with it.

ask.m: We are nearly done. Do you have any questions for me?
o: Yes. When could I start, if you choose me?
What would a typical day be like in this team?
Could you tell me about the salary and the working hours?
br: We would like someone to start next month, if possible.
You would work with four colleagues and help customers by phone and email.
The salary is on the job advert, and the hours are nine to five.

calls.end: Thank you for your time. We will contact you by the end of the week.

calls.title: A faulty product
calls.role: a customer service agent at an electronics shop
phrases: I’d appreciate it if you could…

hi.m: Thank you for calling TechPoint Customer Care. This is Ama. How can I help you today?
o: Hello. I bought a pair of headphones last week, and one side has stopped working.
I am calling about a faulty laptop charger that I bought ten days ago.
Hi, I received a coffee machine yesterday, and it leaks water everywhere.
br: I am sorry to hear that. Sound problems are annoying.
Oh, I am sorry. Let us look into it.
Oh no, that does not sound safe. Let me help.

detail.m: Could you tell me exactly what happened and whether you still have the receipt?
o: It worked fine for two days, then it suddenly stopped. I have the receipt and the box.
It stopped working after I charged it overnight. I have the receipt on my phone.
I am afraid I have lost the paper receipt, but I paid by card, so you can check.
br: No problem. I can find your payment in our system.

options.m: Under our policy, I can offer you a replacement, or a refund to your card. Which would you prefer?
o: I would prefer a full refund, please. I have lost confidence in this model.
A replacement is fine, as long as it arrives quickly. I need it for work.
What are my options if the replacement is also faulty?
br: Of course. The refund will take three to five working days.
We can send a new one by express delivery.
If it fails again, you will get a full refund with no questions asked.

return.m: We will need the faulty product back. How would you like to return it?
o: Could someone collect it from my home? I would rather not go to the post office.
I can drop it off at your shop tomorrow after work.
I would appreciate it if you could send a prepaid label by email.
br: Yes, a courier can collect it. Which day suits you?
That is fine. Just bring the receipt and the product.
I will send the label right now.

close.m: I am sorry again for the inconvenience. Is there anything else I can do?
o: Yes. Could you confirm everything in an email so I have a record?
No, that is fine. Thank you for solving this so quickly.
Just one thing: does the new product have a longer warranty?
br: It has the standard two-year warranty, and I can add one more year free.
Of course. You will receive it within the hour.

calls.end: Thank you for your patience. Have a good day!

calls.title: A proposal in a team meeting
calls.role: a team leader running a short meeting

hi.m: Thanks for joining. You said you have a proposal about how we handle customer emails. Go ahead.
o: I would like to propose a shared inbox, so everyone can see which emails are already answered.
I suggest we answer all emails within four hours. The main benefit is happier customers.
I propose a weekly meeting to share the most difficult cases and learn from them.
br: A shared system could save a lot of time.
Learning from each other is useful.

benefit.m: What is the main benefit, and how much would it cost?
o: The main benefit is that we avoid double answers. The tool costs around twenty dollars a month.
It would cost almost nothing, but it could cut our response time in half.
I do not have exact numbers yet, but I can prepare a short report by Friday.
br: Good. Please include a simple budget in the report.
That is a reasonable price for this team.
That would be a real improvement.

concern.m: One concern: the team is already very busy. Will this not take more of their time at the start?
o: I see your point, but the first week is the only difficult one. After that, we save time.
You are right. Maybe we could train the team for one hour on a quiet afternoon.
That is a fair concern. We could try it for one month and then decide.
br: A trial is a safe way to start. I like that.
One hour is acceptable. Let us find a time.
Hmm, I hope that is true. We will see.

compromise.m: The others are not sure yet. Could you suggest a compromise, so that everyone is comfortable?
o: Could we compromise by starting with only two people for one month, and then review the results?
We could start with the most common questions and add the rest later.
I would be happy to adjust. What would make the team feel comfortable?
br: A small start lowers the risk. Good thinking.
I appreciate the open attitude. I will ask the team.

steps.m: Good. Before we close, could you summarise what happens next?
o: Let us summarise the next steps: I will write a short plan by Friday, and we start the trial on Monday.
First, I send the budget. Second, you get feedback from the team. Third, we decide next week.

calls.end: Great meeting. Let us follow that plan.

calls.title: Telling a friend difficult news
calls.role: a close friend who does not know yet
phrases: I’m afraid I have some difficult news.
I wanted you to hear it from me.
explain why you are telling them
I know this isn’t easy to hear.
I hope you understand my reasons.

hi.m: Hey, you sounded serious in your message. Is everything okay?
o: Not really. I am afraid I have some difficult news, and I wanted you to hear it from me.
I have been putting this off, but I need to be honest with you about something.
It is a bit delicate. Could we find a quiet moment to talk properly?
br: Of course. I am free now. Take your time.
You are worrying me a little. Please go on.
Honesty is always best between friends. Go ahead.

news.m: Okay. I am listening. What is it?
o: I have accepted a job in another country, and I will be leaving in two months.
I have decided to move abroad. It has not been an easy decision for me.
I am afraid I cannot join the business we planned. Something changed in my family.
br: Oh. That is a big change for us. Can you tell me more?
Wow. That is huge. I did not expect it.

reaction.m: I am honestly a bit shocked. Why did you not tell me earlier?
o: I know this is hard to hear. I was waiting for the right moment, and I was afraid of upsetting you.
I am sorry for not telling you sooner. I only got the final answer yesterday.
You are right to be upset. I should have trusted you earlier.
br: Okay. I understand now. That is quick for you too.
Thank you for saying that. It means a lot.
I would rather hear difficult things early, but I understand.

reason.m: Can you help me understand why you made this decision?
o: It is a big chance for my career, and I have wanted something like this for years. I hope you understand my reasons.
It was the trade-off between staying close to the people I love and following a dream. It was not easy.
I felt stuck here. I need a fresh start, though I will miss you very much.
br: I can understand needing a change. Honestly, I have felt that too.
That is a difficult choice. I respect that you thought about it.
You deserve a chance like that, truly.

support.m: I need some time to process this. But I do not want to lose you as a friend.
o: Take all the time you need. Whatever you need, I am here, and we will keep in touch every week.
You will never lose me. Distance changes things, but it does not have to end a friendship.
I understand. Let us meet next week, when you feel calmer, and talk it through properly.
support.re: Thank you. That helps me a lot.

calls.end: Thank you for being honest. Let us not waste the time we have left.
